details: Technology stocks are experiencing a downturn, contributing to the S&P 500's potential for its first consecutive daily decline in three weeks. This market weakness is primarily driven by high bond yields, a consequence of accelerating inflation (reaching its highest in three years) and expectations that the Federal Reserve will maintain elevated interest rates. These macroeconomic pressures are broadly impacting various investments, including cryptocurrencies, with concerns also growing over the potential overvaluation of AI-related stocks.
title: Tech Stocks Fall Amid Inflation & Rate Hike Fears

details: In the week ending June 9, 2026, US spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) recorded approximately US$1.72 billion in net outflows, while Ethereum ETFs saw around US$173 million in withdrawals. This sustained period of institutional capital leaving these digital asset products indicates a worsening risk appetite among investors and has notably diminished a key source of buying pressure for cryptocurrencies.
title: Significant Outflows from US Spot Bitcoin & Ethereum ETFs Continue

details: The market for active tokenized real-world assets (RWA) demonstrated substantial expansion, growing by approximately 589% from early 2025 to June 2026. This growth was notably led by bonds and money market funds in dollar terms, while tokenized public equities showed the fastest percentage increase. This trend suggests a maturing tokenization narrative and increasing institutional demand for yield-generating opportunities within the blockchain ecosystem.
title: Tokenized Real-World Assets Market Shows Strong Growth

details: A Reuters poll conducted on June 10, 2026, revealed that 94% of economists anticipate the Bank of Japan (BoJ) will raise its policy rate to 1.0% during its June meeting. This development accelerates prior expectations for a rate hike and could influence global liquidity and investor sentiment, potentially exerting further downward pressure on various risk assets, including cryptocurrencies.
title: Bank of Japan Expected to Hike Interest Rates to 1.0% in June
